get.description:
Given a domain, path, or url this returns its organic keywords ranked by estimated monthly click value. Prioritizes keywords generating the most traffic based on search volume, ranking position, and click-through rates.

SEO Research

Your competitor's SEO keywords are clues toward what content they're prioritizing and what has slipped. With this SEO tool you can see their rankings and get insights to build your own.
Read how to use this

Endpoint Overview

This endpoint identifies the most valuable organic keywords by calculating estimated traffic value, helping you discover which search terms drive the most visitors to any domain.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Domain or URL to search.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Column to sort by.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: Order to sort the results.

parameters.name: startingRow
parameters.description: Row number to start the results with.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows returned.

parameters.name: countryCode
parameters.description: Country to get results for.

parameters.name: adultFilter
parameters.description: Exclude adult keywords considered unsafe for work.

parameters.name: onlyAdultKeywords
parameters.description: Only include adult keywords considered unsafe for work.

parameters.name: excludeHomepageKeywords
parameters.description: Exclude keywords that rank on the homepage of the searched domain.

parameters.name: keywordDifficulty.min
parameters.description: Filter by Keyword Difficulty

parameters.name: keywordDifficulty.max
parameters.description: Filter by Keyword Difficulty

parameters.name: adCount.min
parameters.description: Filter by the number of total advertisers.

parameters.name: adCount.max
parameters.description: Filter by the number of total advertisers.

parameters.name: searchVolume.min
parameters.description: Filter by the number of searches done this past month on Google.com

parameters.name: searchVolume.max
parameters.description: Filter by the number of searches done this past month on Google.com

parameters.name: includeTerms
parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to be in the results.

parameters.name: includeAnyTerm
parameters.description: Include ANY or ALL terms.

parameters.name: excludeTerms
parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to not be in the results.

keyword.description: When you search a term or phrase (AKA a "keyword"), there are usually thousands of results. If a domain appears within the top 50 results, we consider that search term to be one of its organic (SEO) keywords.

topRankedUrl.description: Highest ranked URL for this keyword

rank.description: A domain's rank is the position that it reached on the SERP for this keyword.

rankChange.description: We compare this ranking to its previous ranking from the time we last saw it. Moving up from position 5 to position 3 is a change of 2.

searchVolume.description: This shows the number of searches done this past month across the US on Google.com (or searches done on Google within the selected country for our other country options). We blend data from multiple sources to give a better snapshot of search activity on this keyword, so it won’t be identical to Google’s metrics for search volume.

keywordDifficulty.description: We’ve calculated how difficult it would be to rank on this keyword. The score is based on a scale of 1-100, 100 being the most difficult to rank for. Compare this number to other keywords you're targeting to get an idea of how to prioritize your SEO campaign.

broadCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

phraseCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

exactCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

seoClicks.description: We estimate that the domain should get this many clicks to its page (per month) based on its current ranking.

seoClicksChange.description: The "change" count shows how many more clicks (or fewer clicks) the domain got from this ranking compared to last month.

totalMonthlyClicks.description: This is the total number of all clicks (organic and paid) made on the SERP over the past month.

percentMobileSearches.description: When we have a breakdown of how many of the searches for this keyword come from mobile vs desktop, we will show it here.

percentDesktopSearches.description: When we have a breakdown of how many of the searches for this keyword come from desktop vs mobile, we will show it here.

percentNotClicked.description: Some SERPs return enough information that the user does not have to click any results. There might also be unexpected results that cause the user to abandon the SERP without any clicks. This is the rate that searchers leave the page without clicking any result.

percentPaidClicks.description: Of all clicks made to this keyword's SERP, this percentage measures how many went to the paid ads.

percentOrganicClicks.description: Of all clicks made to this keyword's SERP, this percentage measures how many went to organic results.

broadMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

phraseMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

exactMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

paidCompetitors.description: This is the total number of advertisers we've seen over the last 14 months for this keyword. It's helpful to know how competitive the field is and how many advertisers have tested this keyword over time.

rankingHomepages.description: This is the number of homepages (from any domain) that rank within the top 100 results for this keyword. A homepage might be "https://webmd.com" vs a longer path like "https://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise."

totalMatchingResults.description:
The total number of results available that matches the query including
items that might not be included in the returned results/page.

parameters.description: Domain or URL to search.

parameters.description: Column to sort by.

parameters.description: Order to sort the results.

parameters.description: Row number to start the results with.

parameters.description: The maximum number of rows returned.

parameters.description: Country to get results for.

parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to be in the results.

parameters.description: Include ANY or ALL terms.

parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to not be in the results.

keyword.description: When you search a term or phrase (AKA a "keyword"), there are usually thousands of results. If a domain appears within the top 50 results, we consider that search term to be one of its organic (SEO) keywords.

topRankedUrl.description: Highest ranked URL for this keyword

rank.description: A domain's rank is the position that it reached on the SERP for this keyword.

rankChange.description: We compare this ranking to its previous ranking from the time we last saw it. Moving up from position 5 to position 3 is a change of 2.

searchVolume.description: This shows the number of searches done this past month across the US on Google.com (or searches done on Google within the selected country for our other country options). We blend data from multiple sources to give a better snapshot of search activity on this keyword, so it won’t be identical to Google’s metrics for search volume.

keywordDifficulty.description: We’ve calculated how difficult it would be to rank on this keyword. The score is based on a scale of 1-100, 100 being the most difficult to rank for. Compare this number to other keywords you're targeting to get an idea of how to prioritize your SEO campaign.

broadCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

phraseCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

exactCostPerClick.description: This is the average amount an advertiser pays Google anytime someone clicks their ad on this keyword. These costs fluctuate depending on many factors, so keep that in mind when you are estimating larger budgets.

seoClicks.description: We estimate that the domain should get this many clicks to its page (per month) based on its current ranking.

seoClicksChange.description: The "change" count shows how many more clicks (or fewer clicks) the domain got from this ranking compared to last month.

totalMonthlyClicks.description: This is the total number of all clicks (organic and paid) made on the SERP over the past month.

percentMobileSearches.description: When we have a breakdown of how many of the searches for this keyword come from mobile vs desktop, we will show it here.

percentDesktopSearches.description: When we have a breakdown of how many of the searches for this keyword come from desktop vs mobile, we will show it here.

percentNotClicked.description: Some SERPs return enough information that the user does not have to click any results. There might also be unexpected results that cause the user to abandon the SERP without any clicks. This is the rate that searchers leave the page without clicking any result.

percentPaidClicks.description: Of all clicks made to this keyword's SERP, this percentage measures how many went to the paid ads.

percentOrganicClicks.description: Of all clicks made to this keyword's SERP, this percentage measures how many went to organic results.

broadMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

phraseMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

exactMonthlyCost.description:
Our estimate of what an advertiser would spend, on average, to advertise on this keyword each month.

We calculate an average cost per click with the estimated number of clicks from the #2 position. Keep in mind that many factors can easily sway these costs.

paidCompetitors.description: This is the total number of advertisers we've seen over the last 14 months for this keyword. It's helpful to know how competitive the field is and how many advertisers have tested this keyword over time.

rankingHomepages.description: This is the number of homepages (from any domain) that rank within the top 100 results for this keyword. A homepage might be "https://webmd.com" vs a longer path like "https://www.webmd.com/fitness-exercise."

totalMatchingResults.description:
The total number of results available that matches the query including
items that might not be included in the returned results/page.

Basic_Authentication_Token.description:
Basic Authentication is a standard that involves encoding your SPYFU_API_ID:SECRET_KEY into a Base64 string. Your SpyFu API ID and Secret Key can both be found under the Account Settings -> API Usage page. Additionally, you can find the Base64 string has been pre-generated on the same page under Base 64 Key. Finally, this encoded string is sent in the "Authorization" header prefixed with the keyword "Basic":
For example, to authorize as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:AB12WXYZ the client would send
Authorization: Basic MDAwMDAwMDAtMDAwMC0wMDAwLTAwMDAtMDAwMDAwMDAwMDAwOkFCMTJXWFla

Query_Parameter_Token.description:
An API key can be added as a query parameter. Your API key is listed as "Secret Key" found under the Account Settings -> API Usage page
For example, to authorize with the API key AB12WXY
/apis/example_api/GetExample?domain=spyfu.com&api_key=AB12WXYZ
Query_Parameter_Token.name: api_key

HMAC_Authentication_Header.description:
For even more security, each request can be individually authenticated with a timestamped HMAC (Hash Message Authentication Code) signature. Composed of your secret key, a valid timestamp, the API request path, and all request parameters.

Creating the signature:


Combine the pieces that will be converted into the signature.
StringToSign =
	HTTP-Verb + "
" +
	Timestamp + "
" +
	UrlPath + "
"
	QueryParameters;

Create UTF-8 encodings of the above string and of your secret key.
byte[] SecretKeyBytes = UTF-8-Encoding-Of( Upper-Case-Of( SECRET_KEY ) );
byte[] StringToSignBytes = UTF-8-Encoding-Of( StringToSign );

Use an implementation of HMAC256 using your UTF-8 secret key to encode the combined string of your request. This should then be converted to Base64 to finish creating your signature.
Signature = Base64( HMAC-SHA256( SecretKeyBytes, StringToSignBytes ) );

Using the signature:


This signature is then sent in through an Authentication header with your username.
Authentication: UserName:Signature
HMAC_Authentication_Header.name: Authentication
